bmp-2bpp.bmp.issue: A 2-bit-per-pixel BMP, legal on Windows CE and read by image-rs in its default mode.

bmp-os2-short-palette.bmp.issue: An OS/2 1.x BMP (12-byte header) whose palette holds fewer than 2^bpp entries, its length set by where the pixels start.

gif-mincodesize-0.gif.issue: A GIF with an LZW minimum code size of 0, which stays refused.

gif-mincodesize-1.gif.issue: A GIF with an LZW minimum code size of 1, read by image-gif, Wuffs, Firefox and Pillow.

ico-large-image.ico.issue: An ICO whose image is 300 pixels wide, so the one-byte directory field holds 44, its low byte. A large icon, not an ambiguous one.

ico-missing-and-mask.ico.issue: A 32-bit icon whose doubled header height promises an AND mask the directory entry does not include. The icon is truncated.

ico-size-mismatch.ico.issue: An ICO whose directory says 16x32 for a 16x16 image, both small enough to encode, so the mismatch is a genuine disagreement readers resolve differently.

jpeg-ac-table-4.jpg.issue: A JPEG scan that selects AC Huffman table 4, past the 0 to 3 a JPEG defines. libjpeg rejects it; the package did not.

jpeg-bad-refinement.jpg.issue: A progressive JPEG scan with Ah=2 and Al=0, where a refinement scan must have Al=Ah-1. libjpeg rejects it; the package did not.

jpeg-trailing-byte.jpg.issue: A valid JPEG with one non-zero byte after EOI: trailing data to strip, not a reason to reject.

jpeg-valid.jpg.issue: A structurally valid baseline JPEG. The package reads no entropy data, so a JPEG whose only fault is one decoder's pixel math is clean.

png-ancillary-bad-crc.png.issue: A PNG ancillary chunk with a stale CRC, which libpng warns past and image-png skips by default. The chunk is dropped, not a reason to reject.

png-bad-color-type.png.issue: A PNG with color type 9, which no decoder defines: a deliberately broken file that stays refused.

png-critical-bad-crc.png.issue: A PNG whose IHDR CRC does not match. A critical chunk with a bad CRC still refuses the file.

png-partial-image.png.issue: A PNG that re-encodes a partially decoded image whole. Nothing in the PNG is cut, so it is clean.

png-pdf-in-pixels.png.issue: A PNG whose compressed pixels decode to bytes that contain %PDF-, but no %PDF- sits in the raw file, so no PDF reader opens it.

png-truncated-idat.png.issue: A genuinely truncated PNG (the IDAT stream is cut and IEND is gone), so the truncation check is shown to catch a real cut.

tiff-extra-tiles.tif.issue: A tiled TIFF whose TileOffsets and TileByteCounts list more tiles than the grid needs, which readers take from the arrays.

tiff-null-entry.tif.issue: A TIFF whose IFD holds a null (type 0) padding entry, which libtiff skips. CR2-style single-strip OJPEG files carry these.

tiff-old-jpeg.tif.issue: A TIFF with old-style JPEG compression whose quantization and Huffman tables live in regions tags 519, 520 and 521 point at. Those regions are image structure, not hidden data.

webp-vp8l-incomplete-code.webp.issue: CVE-2023-4863: a VP8L lossless Huffman code that is incomplete, the kind libwebp's fixed table builder rejects. Decodes no pixels.

webp-vp8l-oversubscribed-code.webp.issue: CVE-2023-4863: a VP8L code-length code that is over-subscribed, the other shape libwebp's fixed table builder rejects.

webp-vp8l-valid.webp.issue: A valid minimal VP8L stream, so the ported libwebp check walks a whole stream without a false positive.
